claims.text: At 673–1273 K, thermally activated dislocation motion in HfNbTaTiZr becomes strongly strain-rate dependent.
Strain-rate-dependent dislocation motion causes measurable variation in yield strength.
Strain-rate-dependent dislocation motion changes the onset of plasticity.
Strain-rate-dependent dislocation motion changes the elastic moduli.
Strain-rate-dependent dislocation motion changes lattice parameters and the inferred thermal-expansion response.
In situ diffraction will reveal increased dislocation density during elevated-temperature deformation.
In situ diffraction will reveal activation of distinct slip systems during elevated-temperature deformation.
Dislocation-density evolution and activation of specific slip systems alter the lattice structure.
Dislocation-density evolution and slip-system activation mediate the macroscopic mechanical response.
Dislocation-density evolution and slip-system activation mediate the thermal-expansion response.
Increasing temperature enhances thermal activation of dislocation motion.
Changes in dislocation density and active slip systems modify lattice spacing.
Changes in dislocation density and active slip systems modify the elastic response.
Relative to room temperature, elevated-temperature yield strength and ductility will vary with strain rate.
Relative to room temperature, elevated-temperature elastic moduli will shift.
Diffraction-measured lattice-parameter changes will correspond to the strain-rate-dependent mechanical changes.
Outside 673–1273 K or 0.0005–0.005 s⁻¹, phase transformations or grain-boundary sliding may dominate.
The proposed comparison uses strain rates from 0.0005 to 0.005 s⁻¹ at 673, 873, and 1273 K.
